name: Nessa Wren
life: Nessa used to promise impossible comforts to people she loved. In nursing school she learned precise language. Her hard days are the ones when precision starts sounding to a family like indifference. On Thursday, near the corner by Juniper Tailor, Nessa looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I promised her we'd try. I kept saying try because of the time I promised my father a trip he never got to make. This time I told the family exactly when to arrive.
appearance: Nessa has short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak, a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, and a favorite piece of clothing, a sand-colored linen shirt. It usually goes with a pen clipped inside the neckline. When somebody else has the floor, Nessa grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Nessa admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Nessa learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To let the patient decide how far to go on the morning.
family: Marc Ramos is Nessa’s cousin’s child. Nessa makes room at the table. Marc brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Saturday keys*, Marc says, “I delivered the missing keys on my skates. It's the first time a grown-up thanked me for using the pavement.”
connections: Cass Pennell. They ask the patient what colors and timing she would want her family to remember.
